title.en: Decision Trees: a Game of Questions
title.bn: ডিসিশন ট্রি: একের পর এক প্রশ্নে লেবেল খোঁজা

summary.en: Follow feature questions from root to leaf and connect each branch with the rectangle it selects on a two-feature plot.
summary.bn: Root থেকে leaf পর্যন্ত ফিচারের প্রশ্নের উত্তর দাও এবং plot-এ প্রতিটি branch-এর অঞ্চল বুঝে লেবেল খোঁজো।

sections.title: Ask a useful question, then ask the next one
A branch keeps the earlier answer
Follow the path and draw its region
Read questions in code and in a fitted drawing
Read the actual iris tree from its root
A tree is a path, not an unordered checklist

examples.title: Grow and follow a tiny two-question tree
examples.explanationHtml: The root asks x ≤ 3. Its left branch asks y ≤ 4.5, while its right branch is already pure class one. Query (2,5) goes left, then right, reaching class one. Five nodes include two questions and three leaves.

examples.title: Verify the same path with DecisionTreeClassifier
examples.explanationHtml: The displayed data have decisive best cuts, so the library tree matches the scratch path, training matches and node count. The educational solver uses feature-order and midpoint-order ties; another tied dataset can legitimately produce a different tree.

examples.title: Read a fitted iris tree drawn by scikit-learn
examples.explanationHtml: The reserved iris flowers are scored after fitting. plot_tree draws the actual learned questions and leaf class counts. Read each test from the root, following its true branch left and false branch right; a leaf stops the path.

practice.title: Follow an explicit two-question fruit tree
practice.statementHtml: Read finite size and sweetness scores from 0 through 6. If size ≤ 3, predict zero when sweetness ≤ 4.5, otherwise one. If size > 3, predict one. Print the class or invalid. Both equality cases follow the ≤ branch.
hints: Only ask the second question after the root answers yes.

practice.title: Count correct paths for a supplied tiny labelled set
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 1 to 20, then n lines x y label with finite coordinates 0–6 and binary labels. Apply the explicit size-three/sweetness-4.5 tree and print correct COUNT of n. Invalid input prints invalid.
hints: The true label scores the answer; it does not choose the branch.
Keep all input validated before reporting a final count.

practice.title: Draw a path-specific cut
practice.statementHtml: Why does the second sweetness cut stop at size three instead of crossing the whole plot?
hints: Keep the parent condition attached to the child.
practice.answerHtml: Only points that answered yes to the root size question reach that child. Its sweetness test subdivides the root-left rectangle, leaving the right region unchanged. Extending the child cut globally would describe a different model.

practice.title: Interpret a mixed leaf
practice.statementHtml: A depth-limited leaf has three class-zero cards and one class-one card. What does its hard prediction mean?
hints: Separate an approximation from ground truth.
practice.answerHtml: It predicts the majority class zero for every query reaching that leaf under the stated tie policy. It does not prove the minority label was wrong. Depth limits can deliberately keep a mixed group, and a training class fraction is not automatically calibrated certainty.

quiz.prompt: Read the tree: where does size two, sweetness five end?
options: Mango directly at the root-right leaf
quiz.explanation: Size two passes the root test, then sweetness five fails the ≤4.5 test, reaching the one-card mango leaf.

caption.en: The fitted two-question tree for eight cards.
caption.bn: আটটি কার্ডে fit হওয়া দুই প্রশ্নের ট্রি দেখো।

quiz.prompt: Read the rectangles: which label does the star at (2,2) receive?
quiz.explanation: The star is left of size three and below sweetness 4.5, inside the class-zero rectangle.

caption.en: Cuts and leaf rectangles from the same fitted tree.
caption.bn: একই fitted ট্রি-এর কাট ও leaf-এর অঞ্চল দেখো।

quiz.prompt: Read the mixed leaf: what is its majority prediction?
options: Apple, without declaring the mango label wrong
quiz.explanation: Three versus one gives apple. A coarse leaf can misclassify a valid minority example.

caption.en: A leaf when the tree stops at depth one.
caption.bn: ট্রি depth একে থামলে বাম leaf-এর count দেখো।

quiz.prompt: Where does a tree query begin?
quiz.explanation: Each answer selects the next branch.

options: The final prediction under that path
quiz.explanation: A leaf stops the question sequence.

quiz.prompt: Which two-feature cut corresponds to one numeric feature test?
quiz.explanation: Testing one feature fixes that coordinate at its threshold.

quiz.prompt: Does a longer path automatically generalise better?
options: No, deeper trees can fit noise
Only if every value is positive
quiz.explanation: Use held-out evidence to choose complexity.

quiz.prompt: Which branch follows equality at the root size threshold?
quiz.explanation: Equality belongs to the stated ≤ branch.

quiz.prompt: Which label follows the explicit two-question tree at (2,5)?
quiz.explanation: Size passes the root, sweetness fails the child, so the leaf is one.

quiz.prompt: How many total nodes have two internal questions and three leaves?
quiz.explanation: All internal and terminal nodes count, giving five.

keyPoints.en: A decision tree follows feature questions from root to leaf.
keyPoints.bn: ডিসিশন ট্রিতে root থেকে leaf পর্যন্ত ফিচারের প্রশ্নের উত্তর দাও।

keyPoints.en: Each child test applies only inside its parent path region.
keyPoints.bn: Child-এর পরীক্ষা শুধু তার parent path-এর অঞ্চলে কাজ করে।

keyPoints.en: A leaf can predict a majority class even when its labels are mixed.
keyPoints.bn: লেবেল মিশ্র থাকলেও leaf তার majority ক্লাস predict করতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: A two-feature numeric test creates an axis-aligned cut.
keyPoints.bn: দুই ফিচারে একটি numeric টেস্ট অক্ষের সমান্তরাল কাট তৈরি করে।

keyPoints.en: Depth controls complexity but does not guarantee unseen accuracy.
keyPoints.bn: Depth দিয়ে জটিলতা বদলায়; নতুন ডেটায় ভালো ফল নিশ্চিত হয় না।

examQuestions.question: Trace size two and sweetness five through the displayed tree.
examQuestions.answerHtml: At the root, two ≤ three is true, so go left. At the child, five ≤ 4.5 is false, so go right to the class-one leaf. The query is predicted mango. The right-of-root region is not visited for this query.

examQuestions.question: Explain the plot region associated with a tree path.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The path x≤3 and y≤4.5 intersects two half-planes, giving the lower-left rectangle. A child cut subdivides only the parent rectangle, so the sweetness line ends at x=3. Leaves assign a label to the resulting regions.

examQuestions.question: Count the matches of a depth-one versus depth-two tree on the eight cards.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The depth-one root splits at x=3. Its left group has three zero labels and one one label, so the majority predicts zero and misses one card; the pure right group predicts one. That gives seven of eight. A second left-side y≤4.5 question separates the remaining exception, giving eight of eight training matches, without proving better future performance.
